sections.h2: How can you sell a house in St. Peters, MO?
sections.html:
You can list the house through an agent, sell it on your own, or take a cash offer from an investor who buys as-is. St. Peters is a suburban city where most homes are owner-occupied, so a conventional listing reaches plenty of buyers, while a cash sale suits houses that need work or owners on a tight schedule.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures show 79.0% of homes lived in by their owners, the highest rate among the four cities in this group. A typical house here is a subdivision home built during the growth years, so the questions buyers ask tend to be about the roof, HVAC, and basement rather than historic details.

  • Agent listing: exposure to financed buyers and the Mid Rivers shopping corridor crowd, with showings and inspection requests.
  • Selling alone: keeps more of the price but leaves the contract and disclosures to you.
  • Investor purchase: shorter timeline and no repair negotiations, with an offer set by the buyer's estimate of the work.

sections.h2: Where did St. Peters come from, and what is it today?
sections.html:
St. Peters grew from farmland into a suburb within a single generation. Wikipedia reports that the city had only 486 people in 1970, about 15,700 by 1980 and 40,660 by 1990. It became a town in 1910 and a city in 1959. The name comes from a Jesuit mission, and a Spanish census from 1791 records an early land grant in the area. When Interstate 70 was built in 1954, crews uncovered the remains of a Mississippian village, which is why a street near the site is called Mound Drive.

Today the city covers 22.37 square miles, all land, northwest of St. Louis on the Interstate 70 corridor. It has the largest shopping center in St. Charles County, Mid Rivers Mall, and the Census Bureau reports 2022 retail sales of $86,224 per resident, far above the other three cities in this group. The population estimate for mid-2025 is 61,479, up 6.5% from the 2020 base.

Amenities that sellers can point to include a park and trail system of more than 1,000 acres, the 236,000 square foot Rec-Plex beside City Hall, and Barnes-Jewish St. Peters Hospital with 175 rooms.

sections.h2: Does St. Peters require an inspection when a home is sold?
sections.html:
No, as long as the home is owner-occupied. The city's Certificate of Occupancy page states plainly that St. Peters does not require an occupancy inspection for the sale of a home that is owner occupied.

The requirement bites for rentals. The city requires a Certificate of Occupancy on any change in use, tenancy or occupancy of a non-owner-occupied single-family house or a multi-family dwelling. A re-occupancy inspection is needed each time the occupant is not the owner on file with the St. Charles County Recorder of Deeds. That covers houses, townhouses, condos, duplexes and apartments, and the inspection can reach all areas of the building.

  • Owner-occupied sale: no city occupancy inspection.
  • Rented house changing tenants: application, fee, inspection and permit.
  • Applications and payments run through the city's CitizenServe portal, with questions at 636-477-6600, extension 1670.

If you are selling a house with a tenant in place, ask the city whether the buyer will need a fresh occupancy permit after closing.

sections.h2: Which school districts cover St. Peters addresses?
sections.html:
Three districts touch the city. The north and northwest parts are in the Fort Zumwalt School District, the southern part is in the Francis Howell School District, and a northeast sliver is in the St. Charles R-VI School District.

Three public high schools sit inside the city limits: Fort Zumwalt South, Fort Zumwalt East and Francis Howell North. Elementary schools named in the city include Fairmount, Hawthorn, Lewis and Clark, Mid Rivers, Progress South, St. Peters and Warren, with DuBray and Fort Zumwalt South Middle School also inside the boundaries. Lutheran High School of St Charles County is a private option within the city. Some St. Peters students attend schools in neighboring Cottleville or O'Fallon, so confirm the assigned school for your exact address with the district.

sections.h2: Where are St. Peters deeds recorded?
sections.html:
St. Peters sits in St. Charles County, so deeds go to the county Recorder of Deeds at 201 N. Second Street in St. Charles, phone 636-949-7900. The fee schedule effective August 28, 2026 lists $23.00 for the first page and $3.00 for each additional page, with a $25.00 charge for non-standard documents. Credit cards carry a convenience fee and personal checks are not accepted.

A title company normally handles the filing. If you are the one recording, such as a lien release you obtained from a lender, call the office first so the document meets the format rules.

City hall can answer questions about local rules at One St. Peters Centre Boulevard, 636-477-6600. St. Peters Board of Aldermen meetings and permit questions go through the same city number.

sections.h2: What does water mean for a St. Peters house?
sections.html:
Heavy rain is the weather event worth planning for. The National Weather Service reported 12.3 inches of rain in St. Peters on July 26, 2022, which Wikipedia describes as an unofficial record. Buyers who saw that flooding may ask about the basement, sump pump and grading, so keep records of any waterproofing or drainage work you have done.

Climate normals for the area show cold winters, with a mean minimum in January of about 3 degrees, and hot summers with mean maximums near 96 degrees. Both extremes put stress on roofs, gutters and cooling systems, and a cash buyer will account for those in the price while a financed buyer may request repairs after inspection.

faqs.q: Is an occupancy inspection needed to sell my house in St. Peters?
faqs.a: No, not for an owner-occupied home. The city says it does not require an occupancy inspection for a sale as long as the property is owner occupied. Rentals changing tenants do need a Certificate of Occupancy.

faqs.q: What school district is St. Peters in?
faqs.a: Several. Fort Zumwalt covers the north and northwest, Francis Howell covers the south, and a northeast sliver belongs to St. Charles R-VI. Confirm the district for your address.

faqs.q: How much does recording a deed cost for a St. Peters house?
faqs.a: The St. Charles County fee schedule effective August 28, 2026 lists $23.00 for the first page and $3.00 per added page, plus $25.00 for non-standard documents.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in St. Peters?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $269,900 for owner-occupied housing units in 2020 to 2024, with median gross rent of $1,321.

faqs.q: Can I sell a St. Peters rental house with a tenant inside?
faqs.a: Yes. The occupancy permit requirement applies when occupancy changes in a non-owner-occupied house, so ask the city at 636-477-6600, extension 1670, what the buyer will need after closing.
